science.title: Spermidine combined with resistance exercise ameliorates myocardial injury and mitochondrial dysfunction via AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α in D-galactose-induced aging rats
science.description: Age-related decline in myocardial structure and function is closely linked to dysregulated mitophagy, impaired mitochondrial biogenesis, and elevated apoptosis. Spermidine (SPD), a naturally occurring polyamine, and resistance exercise (RE) are both known to induce autophagy and exert cardioprotective anti-aging effects. In the present study, we investigated whether combined SPD and RE intervention ameliorates myocardial injury and mitochondrial dysfunction in D-galactose-induced aging rats, and explored the underlying mechanisms. With the exception of a control group, all rats received 6 weeks of daily intraperitoneal D-galactose injections to induce aging. Successful model establishment was verified by quantifying expression of the senescence-associated genes p53, p21, and p16, and by conducting hematoxylin–eosin (H&E) and Masson’s trichrome staining. Following model validation, rats in the aging cohort were assigned to three intervention groups treated for 8 weeks: RE alone, RE + vehicle (VRE), and SPD + RE. Myocardial tissues were assessed using H&E staining, Masson’s trichrome staining, and transmission electron microscopy. Myocardial levels of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), citrate synthase (CS), cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COX I), and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) were quantified. Markers of mitochondrial biogenesis, mitophagy, and apoptosis were also quantified. Molecules of the AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α pathway were measured using reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Combined SPD + RE intervention significantly ameliorated pathological myocardial structural alterations, mitochondrial morphological abnormalities, and functional impairment. It elevated myocardial ATP, CS, COX I, and MMP levels, and activated the AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α pathway. Specifically, it upregulated p-AMPK, SIRT1, PGC-1α, NRF1, and TFAM to promote mitochondrial biogenesis. Enhanced mitophagy was confirmed by an increased LC3B-II/LC3B-I ratio and reduced p62 expression, while suppressed apoptosis was verified by upregulated Bcl-2 and downregulated Bax. In conclusion, combined SPD and RE intervention ameliorates age-related myocardial injury and mitochondrial dysfunction by activating the AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α signaling pathway, promoting mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy, and inhibiting apoptosis.

science.title: Synthesizability, hardness, and stacking order in multicomponent transition metal carbides from machine-learned potentials
science.description: Multicomponent transition metal carbides are promising for extreme-environment applications, but identifying compositions that are both synthesizable and hard remains challenging. We fine-tune the MACE machine-learned interatomic potential on approximately 28,000 density functional theory calculations spanning the composition space of groups 4–6 transition metals and carbon to predict the thermodynamic stability and elastic properties of multicomponent carbides. The fine-tuned model achieves formation energy errors of ~10 meV/atom for thermodynamically relevant structures with only 20% of the training data. We screen over 1500 equiatomic compositions across rocksalt, hexagonal, and hcp prototypes, combining free energy models with elasticity-based hardness surrogates. Synthesizability predictions at 1500 °C agree well with experimental reports for both single-phase and multiphase carbides. The group number of the constituent metals governs both stability and hardness. Short-range order contributes only a few meV/atom to the free energy, so the disordered phase can be treated as a random solid solution when screening rocksalt carbides at high temperature. For compositions mixing group 4/5 and group 6 metals, we identify a new family of stacking-ordered phases with formation energies well below those of disordered rocksalt or hexagonal structures. DFT calculations corroborate these predictions and suggest that stacking-ordered phases should be experimentally accessible in multicomponent carbides. This study provides a framework for screening synthesizable multicomponent materials with target properties, identifies promising carbide compositions across the full nine-component space, and reveals a new class of stacking-ordered carbides accessible only in multicomponent compositions.

science.title: Experimental characterization and scaling of flexural rigidity in sewn multilayer structures
science.description: Sewing is one of the established methods used to fabricate and assemble multilayer insulation (MLI) blankets for aerospace applications, yet the resulting effective flexural behavior remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the room-temperature, quasi-static flexural behavior of MLI blankets composed of aluminized BoPET radiation shields and polyester net spacers across structural configurations of 2, 6, 12, and 24 layers. A full factorial design was employed to evaluate the influence of the number of layers, stitch density, needle thread tension, and needle foot force. Statistical analyses demonstrated that the number of layers is the dominant factor governing flexural response. Among the sewing parameters, needle thread tension was associated with modifications in bending length, while needle foot force primarily affected local compaction. The scaling behavior suggests a provisional transition region in bending resistance, possibly within the 6–12layer range, under the tested conditions. Below this range, the assembly exhibits a lower scaling exponent consistent with weaker interlayer constraint, whereas thicker assemblies show a steeper stiffness increase, indicating enhanced constraint. In contrast, bending length increases uniformly due to its simultaneous dependence on stiffness and mass. Continuous piecewise power-law regression provided a better statistical description of the scaling behavior than conventional single-slope models, reducing the residual sum of squares (RSS) from 2.43 to 1.764 and yielding a lower AICc value. These findings provide a quantitative description of the effective cantilever flexural response of sewn multilayer assemblies at a fixed specimen width under the tested laboratory conditions, offering a basis for manufacturing quality control during handling and assembly.

science.title: Targeted pathway mining reveals novel modified hexapeptides from the demiguisin family
science.description: Following the discovery of the piperazic acid (Piz)-containing hexapeptide demiguisin A from a toxic bird-associated Amycolatopsis strain, we aimed to investigate the structural diversity and bioactive potential of this natural product family. Here, we used the dmg biosynthetic gene cluster from Amycolatopsis sp. PS_44_ISF1 as a pathway mining probe to search for alternative demiguisin A producers. A global search identified only one other soil-derived Amycolatopsis sp. NBC_01488, encoding a highly syntenic pathway. Under feather-mimicking conditions, PS_44_ISF1 demonstrated enhanced growth and metabolite production relative to NBC_01488. Despite phylogenomic distance, both strains produced shared metabolites, while NBC_01488 yielded more abundant demiguisins, enabling the isolation of five novel derivatives characterized by two Piz-moieties with different hydroxylation patterns and glycine truncation. Two congeners displayed potent activity against the avian pathogen Mycobacterium intracellulare and moderate activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. These findings show that targeted pathway mining guided the expansion of the chemical diversity of Piz-modifications and demiguisin congeners with promising anti-Mycobacterium activity.
